Deep learning transformed image recognition [1]. Residual networks made very deep models trainable [2], [3]. Attention mechanisms now dominate language tasks [4]–[5]. A later survey confirmed this [7].

## References

[1] Y. LeCun, Y. Bengio, and G. Hinton, “Deep learning,” Nature, vol. 521, no. 7553, pp. 436–444, 2015, doi: 10.1038/nature14539.
[2] K. He, X. Zhang, S. Ren, and J. Sun, “Deep residual learning for image recognition,” in Proc. IEEE CVPR, 2016, pp. 770–778.
[3] A. Smith and B. Jones, “A residual network that never existed,” IEEE Trans. Imaginary Syst., vol. 3, no. 2, pp. 1–9, 2019.
[4] A. Vaswani et al., “Attention is all you need,” in Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2017, pp. 5998–6008.
[5] J. Devlin, M.-W. Chang, K. Lee, and K. Toutanova, “BERT: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding,” in Proc. NAACL, 2019.
[6] C. Szegedy et al., “Going deeper with convolutions,” in Proc. CVPR, 2015.
